  - N2. minimum_stay_floor_calculation 8.2–8.3 names "party-prevention nights" and that they are "first added together" — the source `result` and the non-factor `party_prevention_nights` binding; kinds and count are not listed.
  - N3. extra_guest_ceiling_calculation §3 "The standard extra-guest share is 0.70 … the share is combined in full first and applied once" — source `baseline.rule` ("the standard extra-guest share") + `result` assembly.
  - N4. extra_guest_damage_loss_addition names "the damage look-back" and party_nights_assessment_record operates on "all of its party-prevention nights added together" — quantities decided by sibling factors, as the source ladders themselves state.

## policy_side_notes (Step 4)
- For listing_ext_pricing_assist_rate, listing_ext_minimum_stay_floor and listing_ext_extra_guest_fee_ceiling, the source's `baseline.rule` ("standard …") and `result` assembly presuppose modifiers (an adjustment total, party-prevention nights, a combined share), so the computation document cannot be fully silent about the existence of variation (N1–N3); a reader is thereby told to look for adjustments, though not which.
- Factor-on-factor design (damage look-back → damage-loss addition; strike/damage/reinstatement nights → assessment-record method) forces one factor document to name another factor's quantity (N4).
- Look-back boundary days ("the last N whole months") stay open as in the source; no record of this task sits on a boundary (strike 2025-06-14 is 15 months back; claims 2025-06-15 and 2026-06-10 are well inside 36 months).
